references.text: The entire congregation of Israel is commanded to take a lamb, showing that the Passover was a communal act for the whole people.
The whole assembled congregation of Israel was to slaughter the lamb, emphasizing the collective nature of the Passover celebration.
The children of Israel are commanded to keep the Passover at the appointed time, confirming that the entire people were to participate in the celebration.
Anyone who fails to keep the Passover shall be cut off from the people, showing the obligatory character of the Passover for the whole congregation.
The children of Israel kept the Passover after entering the promised land, demonstrating the continuation of the Passover commandment for the entire people.
King Hezekiah sent a message to all Israel and Judah to come and keep the Passover, showing that the whole congregation was to participate.
Those who had returned from exile kept the Passover, and the entire congregation took part in the celebration.
Paul refers to Christ as our Passover lamb and urges the whole congregation to celebrate the feast, showing the collective nature of Passover observance in the new covenant.
Both verses establish an eternal covenant for the ritual celebration by the whole congregation through all generations.
Complementary instructions regarding the Passover: who should celebrate (12:47) and when they should celebrate (9:2).
